turns.question: The water temperature on one of our pods has gone jumpy - it steps around by a degree or two between readings while everything else on the same instrument looks steady. Where do we start looking?
turns.answer: Start by checking the temperature sensor itself and its power source. A common cause of erratic temperature readings is a dirty sensor, so clean off any dirt or oil film【1†"Dirty sensor—remove dirt and oil film."】. Also verify the batteries are fresh, since weak batteries can make the sensor “jump”【1†"Weak batteries—replace with new batteries."】. If the sensor’s calibration has expired, recertify or re‑calibrate it【1†"Calibration expired—verify or recertify."】. If those look fine, inspect the wiring: tighten or clean any dirty connections at the meter or sensor【1†"Bad or dirty connection at meter or sensor connections—tighten or clean the connections."】, and look for a broken cable that may need replacement【1†"Break in the cables—replace cables, which may require recertification."】.

Table 6.1–1. 	Troubleshooting guide for temperature measurements.
Symptom 	Possible cause and corrective action
The sensor does not read accurately 	• Dirty sensor—remove dirt and oil film.
• Weak batteries—replace with new batteries.
• Calibration expired—verify or recertify.
Erratic sensor readings 	• Bad or dirty connection at meter or sensor connections—tighten or clean the connections.
• Break in the cables—replace cables, which may require recertification.
• Weak batteries—replace with new batteries.
Readings are slow to stabilize 	• Dirty sensor—clean the sensor to remove dirt and oily film.

turns.question: If it turns out to be the cable, can we just swap it ourselves and carry on?
turns.answer: You can replace the cable, but the guidance notes that doing so “may require recertification”【1†"Break in the cables—replace cables, which may require recertification."】. So swapping the cable is allowed, provided you follow any required recertification procedures afterward.
